summary:
Hemoglobin: 10.0 g/dL; report range: 12.0-16.0 g/dL; below the stated range [1].
White Blood Cell Count: 12000 cells/uL; report range: 4000-11000 cells/uL; above the stated range [1].
Platelets: 250000 cells/uL; report range: 150000-450000 cells/uL; within the stated range [1].
Only supported, readable laboratory rows are analyzed. Verify the results against the original report.
Values outside a stated range are not a diagnosis. Values within range do not guarantee good health.
Educational context: A complete blood count measures different types of blood cells. [2]
Educational context: Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. [2]
Educational context: White blood cells help the body fight infection. [2]
Educational context: Platelets help blood form clots. [2]
Educational context: A CBC result needs interpretation alongside other information about the person. [2]
If you currently have severe symptoms or the report is flagged critical, seek urgent professional assessment; for an emergency contact local emergency services. Verify results with a clinician and the original report.
Discuss with a healthcare professional: Do any of these results need repeat testing? Could my current medicines or recent illness affect these results? How do these results relate to my symptoms and previous tests?
